transcript.text: This could be something simple such as the child lock being on or a supply/isolator issue, but it can also be a failed zone control, element or induction power module. The most useful starting point is to identify the hob type and whether the problem affects every zone or just one. Is it an induction hob, a glass ceramic hob, or solid electric plates — and are all cooking zones affected or only one?
It's a ceramic hob, Zanussi, touch controls. Just the back right ring isn't working, the other three are fine.

With the other three zones working, this is unlikely to be the supply or isolator. The more likely causes are the rear-right radiant element or its zone control; if that zone will not accept a setting at all, the touch-control/PCB side becomes more likely. With the hob cool, switch it off at the isolator, wipe the glass and touch-control area fully dry, then restore power and try the zone once more. When you select the rear-right zone and set a heat level, does its display show and hold the selected number, or does it refuse/cancel it?
Yes the number shows when I pick that ring, it holds it fine. It just never glows red or gets hot though.

The most likely cause is a failed radiant element (or its connection/thermal protection); less commonly, that zone’s output circuit on the control board has failed. As a final safe check, switch the hob off at the cooker isolator for five minutes, restore power, then try that zone again with the glass dry. If it still displays a level but stays completely cold, it will need an engineer: internal hob repairs involve mains wiring and dismantling under the glass.

candidates: Fault with a cooking zone, control or power module (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "not working properly". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit.
